record.category: checkout / payment processor used by Brazilian and Spanish-language resellers

free_tier.stated: Not a service bought from the vendor. Hotmart charges the seller; the buyer pays the product price, with 'taxas especificas que podem ser aplicadas a compras internacionais e de produtos digitais'.

record.interface_detail: A hosted checkout that adapts by country and converts currency automatically: 'o checkout da Hotmart faz a conversao automatica do valor do seu produto para a moeda do seu comprador'. The seller chooses which methods to enable per product.
record.tooling: Browser only, plus subscription and installment products. No client needed.
record.chaining: Hotmart is the Spanish- and Portuguese-language checkout most likely to be in front of a reseller that also sells to Spain, Mexico or Argentina, because it settles in more than 180 countries and converts the price. It is the payment path a foreigner is most likely to complete without a Brazilian document.

limits.value: method availability is set per product by the seller and varies by buyer country; Pix and boleto are listed as Brazil-only

record.limits_note: The article states that not all methods reach all buyers: 'cada pais possui taxas especificas que podem ser aplicadas a compras internacionais'.
record.binding_note: The gate is which methods the seller enabled and which ones the buyer's country allows; a card is the only method that crosses both.

identity_cost.detail: Email plus a card. The global card section asks only for 'numero do cartao, nome do titular, data de vencimento e CVV'.

record.reliability_note: Installments are charged once by Hotmart and split by the buyer's bank, so a refund does not cancel the installments directly with the issuer: 'Depois da aprovacao, nao e possivel cancelar as parcelas diretamente com a operadora.'
record.confidence_note: The method inventory, the 180-country reach, the global card fields and the Pix-is-Brazil-only classification were read in Hotmart's own help article, updated 2026-10-19.

evidence.proved: 'mais de 20 metodos de pagamento, alcancando compradores em mais de 180 paises'
'Metodos de pagamento exclusivos do Brasil > Pix', which places Pix on the Brazilian side of the divide
the global card path and the installment caveat: 'nao e possivel cancelar as parcelas diretamente com a operadora'

record.notes: Documented as a rail, not as a provider: its role among debrid providers is to answer whether a foreigner can pay a Brazilian or Spanish reseller. The answer is yes by card, in a converted currency, subject to the seller having enabled a global method for that product.

free_tier.stated: 'Each article has no limit on overall storage or total number of attached files.' Per-file 20 MB. But account-level file storage is separately capped at 10 GB base + 2 GB/agent (Team). The article-level 'no limit' sits inside that account bucket.

egress.terms: Free and unranged-open. Article attachments are served from `support.zendesk.com/hc/article_attachments/<id>` with no auth, no referer check, `Accept-Ranges: bytes`, `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` permissive, `x-amz-replication-status: COMPLETED`, AES256 at rest.

record.tooling: Help Center API (`/api/v2/help_center/articles/{id}/attachments.json` returns the public `content_url`). Third-party CLI `tukaelu/zgsync` adds a Guide media subcommand.
record.chaining: 20 MB per file x unbounded attachments per article, but the 10 GB account file-storage pool is the wall. Trial-only for a free account, so the multiplier is trial instances, which is a bad trade.
record.limits_note: Per-object-cap: 20 MB per file/image in articles (2 MB for community images). Quota: account file storage 10 GB base + 2 GB/agent. request-rate: Guide API is rate limited; an unauthenticated write probe `POST /api/v2/help_center/articles.json` returned 403 (good. No open write). Retention: archived tickets still count toward storage.
record.reliability_note: The read path is the cleanest in this whole niche. Public, ranged, unauthenticated, no expiry. But Zendesk has no free plan (14-day trial), so it cannot be a free-storage answer, only a pattern to copy.

evidence.proved: ... — 'Articles: 20MB limit per file or image upload' and 'Each article has no limit on overall storage or total number of attached files'
default storage '10 GB base' + '2 GB per agent' (Team)
probe: GET -> 200, 365,146 bytes, image/png, no referer/UA needed (also 200 with `curl/8`), `Range: bytes=0-99` -> 206
probe: 8 parallel ranged GETs x 45,000 B -> all 206, 360,000 B in 0.63 s

record.notes: 'Each article has no limit on overall storage or total number of attached files.' Per-file 20 MB. But account-level file storage is separately capped at 10 GB base + 2 GB/agent (Team). The article-level 'no limit' sits inside that account bucket.
